overview: Sigma 4.11's Highjump is a five-mode vertical launcher: Mineplex, AAC, Basic, Cubecraft and Hypixel. Cubecraft mode opens with a 99-packet C04 burst: while grounded it sends 49 pairs of (y plus 0.0625, onGround false) followed by (y, onGround false), then one (y, onGround true) closer, and sets motionY to 2.2, re-running the whole burst on every landing when the TOGGLE auto-disable setting is off. Mineplex mode probes for a ledge ahead of the player with getBestMineplexExploit (scanning yOff from -1.5 down to -9), teleports there with a C04 pair (base position then lifted position, both onGround true), applies the BOOST motionY (default 3.0) and disables itself on any incoming S08 lag-back. AAC stages five pre-computed motionY values (0.3609, 0.2902, 0.2210, 0.1379, 0.055) after a jump, Basic overwrites the EventJump motion with the BOOST value, and Hypixel accumulates fall distance past 9 to trigger a 0.28 horizontal pin plus the boost. onDisable restores timerSpeed to 1 and re-pins motion to 0.2.

sections.p: The module registers EventUpdate, EventPacket and EventJump handlers with per-mode state: stage, speed, fall, jumped and groundTicks. onEnable seeds stage to -1 and, for Cubecraft mode, runs the ground burst immediately when MoveUtils.isOnGround(0.001) and isCollidedVertically hold; otherwise it sets stage to 999. onDisable re-pins motion to 0.2 through the private setMotion and restores mc.timer.timerSpeed to 1. The settings are MODE (Mineplex, AAC, Basic, Cubecraft, Hypixel), BOOST (a Number with default 3.0, increment 0.1, bounds 1 to 10) and TOGGLE (auto-disable on landing, default true).

Cubecraft is a teleport-burst mode. On a grounded start it loops 49 times, each iteration sending a C04 position packet at y plus 0.0625 with onGround false and then a C04 at y with onGround false, followed by a single C04 at y with onGround true, all through NetworkManager.sendPacketNoEvent: 99 packets in one tick, then motionY 2.2 and stage set to -2. In the air it re-lifts with motionY 0.42 at stage 0, pins horizontal speed as 0.46 minus stage over 200, and when falling past -0.2 drops timerSpeed to 0.3 and alternates setMotion(1.9) and setMotion(0.3) with the fall-distance-scaled dampener, restoring timerSpeed to 1 on landing. With TOGGLE off, the landing branch repeats the 99-packet burst and the 2.2 launch while groundTicks counts up.

sections.h: Mineplex ledge exploit and staged modes
sections.p: Mineplex mode builds a 0.6 by 2 block probe box at the next position derived from the movement input, requires the box one block below to be empty, and calls getBestMineplexExploit, which steps yOff down by 0.5 from -1.5, requiring a solid cell below, an empty probe box and an empty box at minus 0.5, until yOff passes -4.5 or -9. On a found ledge it queues C04 p2 (base position, onGround true) then C04 p1 (base plus the ledge offset, onGround true), so the server ends the tick at the lifted position with a true ground flag, sets the local position and event x/z, and applies motionY equal to BOOST. AAC applies 0.3609 at stage 0 only when motionY exactly equals 0.3479000067710857, then 0.2902, 0.2210, 0.1379 and 0.055 in the following stages. Basic overwrites the EventJump pre motion with the BOOST value, and Hypixel accumulates the negative motion into fall and triggers setMotion(0.28) plus the boost once the accumulated fall passes 9, with the posY floor check gating repeats.

files.label: Highjump.java
files.explanation: All five modes, the 99-packet Cubecraft burst with its landing re-arm, the getBestMineplexExploit ledge probe and the p2-then-p1 C04 send order, the AAC exact-equality guard, the Hypixel fall accumulator, the S08 lag-back self-disable in Mineplex mode and the onDisable resets. The imported C08PacketPlayerBlockPlacement is unused in this file.

files.label: MoveUtils.java (shared motion engine)
files.explanation: The private setMotion in the module mirrors MoveUtils.setMotion's yaw decomposition, and every mode leans on MoveUtils.isOnGround (0.001 and 0.4 variants) and defaultSpeed. Because the module writes motion fields rather than packets, the launch reaches the server through the regular C03 position stream; the same utility backs the Sigma Bhop, Fly and Step modules.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (vertical envelope)
countering.explanation:
NCP SurvivalFly rebuilds the allowed vertical movement from the world instead of the packet. vDistRel carries the allowance from the previous move's momentum and accepts only the named envelopes: a zero-y move on ground, a real jump (isJumpMotion arms a 10-tick jumpDelay), a step-up and a riptide launch, with both ground flags coming from the block cache via RichBoundsLocation.isOnGround rather than the packet flag. The Cubecraft burst's single onGround true closer over open air is ignored because the ray trace finds air, and the Mineplex C04 pair is a one-tick y jump of several blocks with a fake ground claim, so yDistanceAboveLimit lands far beyond the envelope and the (hAbove plus yAbove) times 100 violation fires with a set-back.

The honest caveat is the burst's first packet: the 49 false-flag pairs sit at the current y and y plus 0.0625, a sub-move jitter that the envelope sees as near-zero deltas, so the burst itself does not flag; the 2.2 launch that follows it does, on the first air move. The AAC staged ladder, by contrast, is tuned as a decaying jump arc and is the mode closest to the envelope's tolerance.

countering.label: MorePackets (movement packet rate)
countering.explanation:
NCP MorePackets counts the raw serverbound move rate, content-blind, invoked per move from MovingListener. Each move scores into morePacketsFreq, an ActionFrequency with 500ms buckets over the configured window against the ~22 packets per second ceiling (20 ideal), and a separate burst path flags 15 packets in the newest half-second bucket with a direct-violation threshold of 10.

The Cubecraft mode is a direct target: 99 C04s in one tick is about 6 times the burst threshold and saturates the window accumulator on the first tick, a direct violation and cancel at the default action level, and the burst repeats on every landing while TOGGLE is off. The Mineplex C04 pair adds only 2 packets per jump and stays under the rate windows; among the five modes only the Cubecraft burst crosses the rate model, which is exactly the fingerprint that separates it from the others.

countering.label: Flight (ascension bounds)
countering.explanation:
Arc v2's Flight check classifies vertical motion into states. The rising branch fires whenever the measured vertical speed exceeds getMaxJump, the configured maximum legitimate jump velocity: that is the Ascension violation with the ascending_vertical message, and sustained ascent also trips the ascending_moves time bound and the ascending_distance distance-from-ground bound.

The Cubecraft and Mineplex launches set motionY between 2.2 and 3.0, roughly five to seven times the vanilla 0.42 jump, so the first air move after the launch flags. The Mineplex C04 teleport itself is a position jump rather than velocity, which Arc's movement listener treats as a discontinuity, and the AAC staged ladder (0.36, 0.29, 0.22, 0.14, 0.055) mimics a decaying jump arc and is the one mode tuned to stay near the envelope; the descending side expects a gravity polynomial, and any deviation beyond 0.02 or below 0.001 in the glide term flags descend_expected when the boosted arc comes down.

countering.label: Fly (per-player vertical simulation)
countering.explanation:
Hawk's Fly check runs a per-player vertical simulation of the 1.8 gravity model. Each air tick the estimated velocity becomes the previous estimate minus 0.08 times 0.98, integrated into an estimated position, and any discrepancy between the reported y and the estimate above DISCREPANCY_THRESHOLD (0.0001) triggers punishAndTryRubberband. A vanilla jump launches at 0.42 and the simulation tracks it exactly, which is why ordinary jumps pass.

The module's 2.2 to 3.0 launches against a predicted 0.42 first-tick velocity are discrepancies of roughly 1.8 to 2.6, thousands of times the threshold, so the check flags and rubber-bands on the first air move. The AAC staged values drift off the gravity curve from the second stage onward, and the Mineplex teleport lift never appears in the simulation at all, so the position discrepancy is even larger. The module ships no concealment that could pull the reported stream back onto the simulation's curve.
